Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

  REGULAR MEETING
  MONDAY, MAY 2, 2022 – 6:30 P.M.

The City Council of the City of Azusa met in Regular session at the above date and time in the Azusa Auditorium located
at 213 E. Foothill Blvd., Azusa, CA 91702.

Mayor Gonzales called the Regular meeting to order at 6:30 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: BECKWITH, AVILA Jr., ALVAREZ, MAYOR PRO-TEM MENDEZ, MAYOR
GONZALES
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS:

Services Johnson, Director of Public Works/City Engineer Delgadillo, Deputy City Manager DeAnda-Scaia, Director of
Community Resources Carpenter, Director of Economic & Community Development Marquez, IT and Library Services
Director Graf, Economic Development Specialist Campos, and Chief Deputy City Clerk Garcia.

None

1.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATORS – Pursuant to California Government
  Code, Section 54956.8.

  City Negotiators: Sergio Gonzalez, City Manager and Matt Marquez, Director of Economic & Community

  Under Negotiation: Price and Terms

2.  GRIEVANCE REVIEW – Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 –

  Review of Employee Grievance and Complaint Pursuant to Sections 15.4 and 15.6 of the City’s Rules of the
  Civil Service System.

REGULAR SESSION

Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 7:30 P.M.

CITY COUNCIL ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: BECKWITH, AVILA Jr., ALVAREZ, MENDEZ, GONZALES
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayra Rico and Charlotte.
 Invocation was delivered by James Abraham of Winters Outreach Church.

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo.

Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, City Attorney Marco, Chief of Police Wenrick, Director of Administrative
Services Johnson, Director of Public Works/City Engineer Delgadillo, Deputy City Manager DeAnda-Scaia, Director of
Community Resources Carpenter, Director of Economic & Community Development Marquez, IT and Library Services
Director Graf, Economic Development Specialist Campos, and Chief Deputy City Clerk Garcia.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

City Attorney Marco stated City Council met in Closed Session for two items and there were no reportable actions.

CEREMONIAL

1. Mayor Pro Tem Mendez provided Presentation of Proclamation proclaiming May 2022 as ‘Older Americans
  Month’ in the City of Azusa.

2. Councilmember Alvarez provided Presentation of Proclamation proclaiming May 2022 as ‘Physical Fitness and
  Sports Month’ in the City of Azusa.

3. Councilmember Avila Jr. provided Presentation of Proclamation proclaiming May 1-7, 2022 as ‘Public Services
  Recognition Week’ in the City of Azusa.

4. City Clerk Cornejo provided Presentation of Proclamation proclaiming May 1-7, 2022 as the ‘53rd Annual
  Municipal Clerks Week’ in the City of Azusa.

5. Councilmember Beckwith provided Presentation of Proclamation proclaiming May 1-7, 2022 as ‘National Small
  Business Week’ in the City of Azusa.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Mayra Rico provided comment about the Azusa Rotary Field of Glory event.

Paul Hernandez with Water Education for Latino Leaders provided comment about a conference in June 10th
about Water Policy changes and financial resources.

Pastor James Abraham provided comments regarding his published book and presented one for each member of
City Council.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Gonzalez provided a PowerPoint presentation regarding the status of Council’s direction from the Special
Council meeting that took place on how to best allocate City Accomplishments from the City’s Reserve Funds and
commented the current drought situation and possible future water restrictions will be on the next Utility Board meeting
Agenda and reminded residents that any early conservation methods would be of help.

City Council Communications

Mayor Pro-Tem Mendez thanked Mayra Rico and Charlotte for leading the Flag Salute, thanked Paul Hernandez for the
invitation to the well event and congratulated Miss Ginger for her time at Azusa and her future endeavors.

Councilmember Alvarez commented he attended the most recent Foothills Transit Authority meeting and announced the
cancellation of lines 690 and the route variant of Line 292, Foothills Transit Authority is looking to purchase twenty-four
double-decker zero emissions buses by Fiscal Year 2023 by using a Grant of $31 million dollars. Ridership continues to
increase; LA County extended the mask mandate for public transit services.

Azusa City Council Minutes May 2, 2022  Page 2
 Councilmember Avila Jr. announced April 20th was the State of the City Address and thanked everyone involved with
pulling off the event. April 23rd for Arbor day 50 trees were planted by over 100 volunteers with many thanks to all the
sponsors and people who helped, thanks to all the staff in honor of Proclamation for Public Services week, Thursday May
5th will be a collaboration with Google and Canva for a Boost your Business Brand Building event in the Library
Auditorium, and Happy Mother’s Day to all mothers in the City.

Councilmember Beckwith thanked Mayra for announcing the Field of Glory event and said it’s a great event, thanked the
staff for all their work in recognition of Public Services week.

Mayor Gonzales wished all mother Happy Mother’s Day, commented about the upcoming School Board meeting
regarding the closing of Rockvale Avenue for the High School and asked City Manager to provide further clarity. City
Manager Gonzalez explained how that transpired, he was asked to provide the School Board with information on how to
go about getting the road closed in the future, should that be considered an option for additional safety for students
crossing the road. Mayor Gonzales commented on recreational park bathrooms complaints and requested that be a topic at
a future Council meeting as an Agenda item and commented about the community meeting he attended regarding the
Foothill Vista mobile home park about rent stabilization and requested the 30-year-old ordinance regarding rent
stabilization also be brought back to a future Council meeting as an Agenda Item for updating. City Attorney Marco stated
most of the work has been done and Council will be seeing that Ordinance in an updated version soon. Lastly Mayor
Gonzales announced Azusa Connects has created a bowling fundraiser and they are looking for bowlers to represent
Azusa in a multi-city bowling competition with 7 other cities on May 26th in El Monte, the bowler must be staff or
elected. Proceeds will be donated to the One Legacy Event a week later.

SCHEDULED ITEMS

1.  FIRST READING – ORDINANCE REVISING CHAPTER 2, ARTICLE III – TEMPORARY
  APPOINTMENTS.

  1) Waive further readying, read by title only, and introduce Ordinance No. 2022-02. AN ORDINANCE OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AZUSA AMENDING CHAPTER 2, ARTICLE III,
  SECTION 2-194 OF THE AZUSA MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO TEMPORARY
  APPOINTMENTS

Director of Administrative Services Johnson explained the Ordinance.

Motion by Councilmember Avila Jr. to move First Reading – Ordinance No. 2022-02 revising Chapter 2, Article III –
Temporary Appointments and waive further readying and read by title only, seconded by Councilmember Beckwith, and
carried by unanimous vote of City Council.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: AVILA Jr., MENDEZ, GONZALES, ALVAREZ, BECKWITH
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSTAIN:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

2.  DISCUSSION REGARDING 2022 SUMMER MEETING SCHEDULE.

  1) Discuss and provide direction to Staff.

City Clerk Cornejo began discussion with historical summer schedule information. Utility meetings will remain as
scheduled. July, August, and September will have one City Council meeting per month unless an emergency meeting is
needed, the first meeting of each month will be canceled.

CONSENT CALENDAR

1. Minutes of the Special meeting January 24, 2022 and March 28, 2022 were approved as written.

2. Resolution No. 2022-C33 allowing certain claims and demands and specifying the funds out of which the same
  are to be paid was approved.

3. Personnel Action Requests in accordance with the City of Azusa Civil Service Rules and applicable
  Memorandum of Understanding(s) was approved.

4. A Letter of Agreement with the Azusa Unified School District to fund eight weeks of summer programming for
  the 2022 summer, with an option to extend through the summer of 2023; and Authorize the City Manager to
  execute the Agreement, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney, on behalf of the City, subject to non-
  substantive changes made by City Manager and City Attorney was approved.

Azusa City Council Minutes May 2, 2022  Page 3
 5. Accept the grant award from California Library Literacy Services (CLLS); and Approve necessary budget
  amendments and adjust the current fiscal year budget accordingly was approved.

6. Resolution No. 2022-C34 setting the number of transitional fireworks sales permits available for 2022 at two (2)
  was approved.

7. The Second Amendment to the Maintenance Services Agreement between the City of Azusa and Crosstown
  Electrical & Data Inc.; and Authorize the City Manager to execute the Contract Amendment, in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney, on behalf of the City was approved.

8. The purchase of a security camera system from LensLock Incorporated in an amount not to exceed $99,915.00
  in year (1) one and a total not to exceed $164,245.86 over the 48-month contract period; and Approve the
  purchase of this product as authorized under AMC Section 2-520(b) was approved.

9. Accept the project improvements; and Authorize Staff to file a Notice of Completion for the Structured Cabling
  Infrastructure project was approved.

Motion by Councilmember Avila Jr. to approve the Consent Calendar items 1 - 9, seconded by Councilmember Beckwith,
and carried by unanimous vote of City Council.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: AVILA Jr., MENDEZ, GONZALES, ALVAREZ, BECKWITH
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSTAIN:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

SECOND READING ORDINANCES

1.  SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 2022-01 ADDING SECTION (7) TO ARTICLE VII,
  SECTION 18-532 OF THE CITY OF AZUSA MUNICIPAL CODE TO AUTHORIZE LIMITED
  ESTATE SALES TO BE CONDUCTED IN THE CITY OF AZUSA.

  1) Read by title only, second reading and adoption, Ordinance No. 2022-01;

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AZUSA, CALIFORNIA, ADDING
  SECTION (7) TO ARTICLE VII, SECTION 18-532 OF THE CITY OF AZUSA MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  AUTHORIZE LIMITED ESTATE SALES TO BE CONDUCTED IN THE CITY OF AZUSA

Motion by Councilmember Avila Jr. to adopt Ordinance No. 2022-01 Adding Section (7) to Article VII Section 18-532 of
the City of Azusa Municipal Code, seconded by Mayor Pro-Tem Mendez, and carried by unanimous vote of City Council.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: AVILA Jr., MENDEZ, GONZALES, ALVAREZ, BECKWITH
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSTAIN:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

ADJOURNMENT

It was the consensus of the Council to adjourn the meeting in solemn honor of those Azusans who lost their lives to
Covid-19 and in memory of Lucy Avila Villatoro and Pierre Domingo Royere who were both lifelong residents.

TIME OF ADJOURNMENT: 8:16 P.M.
